headline: Conquer the cold with the Polar Peak range
standfirst: Science-backed winter gear for serious campers
brief: Polar Peak has paid for this page, but our readers trust us. The trading standards office has asked us to check every scientific claim.

body.t: The Polar Peak parka is packed with our Thermo-Fill lining, which stops the cold from getting in.

options: “Cold” does not move: thermal energy transfers from the warm body outwards, and the lining slows it.
The lining should be stopping the cold from getting out, not in.
A lining cannot affect how quickly a person cools down, because the body and the air stay at the same temperatures whatever is worn.
feedback: There is still no such thing as “cold” moving in either direction. Think about what actually transfers, and which way.
Insulation really does slow the transfer of thermal energy. The problem is the description of what is being transferred.
err.fix: The Polar Peak parka is packed with our Thermo-Fill lining, which slows the transfer of thermal energy from your warm body to the cold air outside.
keys: Thermal energy is transferred from hotter to colder.
The lining reduces the rate of transfer; “cold” does not travel.

body.t: Thousands of tiny air pockets in the lining help, because trapped air is a poor thermal conductor and cannot carry energy away by convection.
body.ok: It is correct: air conducts poorly, and trapping it in small pockets prevents convection currents.

body.t: Our two-litre hot-water bottle is twice the size of the leading brand, so it holds twice as much temperature to see you through the night.

options: A bigger bottle holds less temperature, because the same energy from the kettle is spread out through more water molecules.
Temperature is not stored: at the same temperature, twice the mass of water has twice the internal energy.
Two litres of water would be twice as hot as one litre.
feedback: Temperature is not stored in the first place, so it can't be more or less “held”.
Water from the same kettle is at the same temperature, however much of it there is.
err.fix: Our two-litre hot-water bottle is twice the size of the leading brand, so at the same temperature it stores twice as much internal energy to see you through the night.
keys: Temperature and energy are different quantities.
The larger mass stores more internal energy at the same temperature.

body.t: Water has an unusually high specific heat capacity, so it releases a lot of energy for every degree that it cools.
body.ok: It is correct: water's specific heat capacity is about 4200 J per kg per kelvin, high compared with most common materials.

body.t: A full bottle, holding two kilograms of water, gives out about 84 kilojoules of energy as it cools by 10 °C.
body.ok: It is correct: $Q = mc\Delta T = 2 \times 4200 \times 10 = 84\,000$ J, which is 84 kJ.

body.t: The Polar Peak steel flask has a vacuum between its double walls, which blocks all three kinds of thermal energy transfer: conduction, convection and radiation.

options: A vacuum is a very good conductor, so conduction is not blocked.
Convection is the transfer a vacuum cannot stop, because hot air always rises.
A vacuum stops conduction and convection, but radiation needs no medium and can cross it.
feedback: With no particles to pass on the energy, a vacuum cannot conduct.
Convection needs a fluid that can move. In a vacuum there is no fluid at all.
err.fix: The Polar Peak steel flask has a vacuum between its double walls, which prevents conduction and convection across the gap, and shiny walls reduce radiation, which can still cross a vacuum.
keys: A vacuum prevents conduction and convection.
Radiation can cross a vacuum (shiny surfaces only reduce it).

body.t: Our TurboFlame stove brings a pan of water to the boil in under four minutes.
Leave it on full power, and the boiling water will carry on getting hotter and hotter, so your pasta cooks in half the time.

options: While water boils, its temperature stays at the boiling point; the energy changes liquid to vapour.
Boiling water does get hotter, but only very slowly, because most of the energy supplied escapes with the steam.
Boiling water cools down, because the fastest molecules leave.
feedback: At a fixed pressure, the temperature of boiling water stays constant, however fast the energy is supplied.
Evaporation can cool a liquid, but here the stove keeps supplying energy, and the temperature stays at the boiling point.
err.fix: Leave it on full power and the water will boil away faster, but it will stay at its boiling point, so your pasta will not cook any quicker.
keys: The energy supplied goes into the change of phase (it increases the potential energy of the molecules).

body.t: Finally, the CloudRest air mattress is made to keep its shape all night, and you can pump it up in under a minute.
Other mattresses go soft on cold nights because the air molecules inside shrink, but our patented valve lets you top it up in seconds.

options: The molecules shrink, but that is not why the pressure falls: the valve is leaking, so air escapes during the night.
The molecules do not shrink: in the cold they move more slowly on average, so the pressure on the walls falls.
The molecules stop moving altogether in the cold, so the air exerts no pressure.
feedback: Molecules do not change size when a gas cools. Nothing in the advert suggests a leak.
Molecules only have very little motion near absolute zero. On a cold night they are still moving at hundreds of metres per second.
err.fix: Other mattresses go soft on cold nights because the air molecules inside move more slowly on average, so they exert less pressure on the walls, but our patented valve lets you top it up in seconds.
keys: Lower temperature means lower average kinetic energy, so less frequent and gentler collisions and a lower pressure.
